pitchei_teshuva.he: לכנסו לכיפה. עיין בתשובת נודע ביהודה חיו"ד סימן פ"א שכתב דהטעם הוא משום הפסד כהן ולפ"ז בספק בכור שאפילו במומו אין צריך ליתנו לכהן כי המע"ה רשאי לכנסו לכיפה אך הגאון מוהר"ם פישלש ז"ל נחלק עליו וחזר בו המחבר והודה לדבריו לאסור הכנסה לכיפה אפילו בספק בכור ע"ש בסימן ס"ב ופ"ג. [ועיין בת' חתם סופר ס"ס שי"ד וס"ס שי"ח מ"ש בזה]:
pitchei_teshuva.en: To place it into a confined enclosure. See Responsa Noda BiYehudah, Yoreh Deah siman 81. He initially writes that the reason is concern for the kohen's financial loss. Accordingly, with a doubtful firstborn, which even after developing a blemish need not be given to a kohen because the burden of proof rests on the claimant, the owner could confine it. The gaon Maharam Fischels disagreed, and Noda BiYehudah later retracted and agreed that even a doubtful firstborn may not be placed into such an enclosure. See simanim 82 and 83. See also Responsa Chatam Sofer at the ends of simanim 314 and 318.

Rosh.
נחתך הזנב למעלה מן החוליא הוי מום. אבל מן החוליות ולמטה לצד שער הזנב לא הוי מום: **** ENGLISH **** If the tail was cut off above the joint it is a blemish; but from the joints downward toward the hair of the tail it is not a blemish.
ועוד מנה בעל הטור כו'. עיין בעט"ז שהביא כל המומין שהם מומין אליבא דכ"ע וביאורן: **** ENGLISH **** And furthermore the author of Tur listed, etc. — see Taz who brought all the blemishes that are blemishes according to all opinions and their explanations.
siftei_kohen.en: Nowadays, when there is no expert. An expert must also be proficient in visual examination, inspecting and scrutinizing blemishes thoroughly. Moreover, an expert means one who received authorization from the nasi in Eretz Yisrael to permit firstborn animals on the basis of blemishes, and nowadays there is no nasi in Eretz Yisrael. Rosh.

baer_heitev.en:
The tragus. In the chapter Metzora, Rashi explains this as the middle ridge of the ear, meaning the raised portion in the middle of the ear that forms a kind of partition before the ear canal. Taz. The "edge of the ear" means the soft earlobe, called skin, where healthy flesh returns. Rashi writes so.

והאידנא כו'. הרא"ש ותוס' שם ד"ה פסק ומיהו כו' משום שצריך שיהיה חכם גדול ובקי גם בראיית מומין וזש"ש לענין נדר חכם ולענין בכור מומחה וערא"ש שם ועוד כתב ב"י טעם משום דליכא נשיא בא"י ליטול ממנו רשות והוא ע"פ מ"ש הרמב"ם רפ"ג אין כו' ע"פ המומחה שנתן לו הנשיא שבא"י רשות כו' ונראה שדקדק מהנ"ל דקרי ליה מומחה וכמ"ש בריש סנהדרין לענין קנסות דבעינן מומחין וכבר כ' שאין ראיה וה"נ אמר שם (ה' א') לענין דן יחידי מומחה ואמרינן שם אע"ג דלא נטל רשות ועוד נראה שדקדק ממ"ש בבכורות שם התרת בכור בח"ל כו' וז"ש רמב"ם שם וכן בכור שיצא ח"ל כו' אבל רש"י פי' שם ד"ה בח"ל שאינו ראוי כו' וכן אין לדקדק מהא דפ"ק דסנהדרין (ה') דאמר יתיר בכורות דה"נ קאמר יורה כו' וכמש"ש וכיון דגמיר כו' משום מעשה כו' ודוקא בתלמיד וכמש"ל סי' רמ"ב ס"ד אלא שי"ל מירושלמי (פ"א דחגיגה ופ"י דנדרים) שבקש רב מר"ג ברבי לאחר מיתת אביו שיתן לו רשות להתיר בכורות ואחר מיתת רבו א"צ רשות וביומא ע"ח א' שאלו את ר"א זקן כו' דבר זה הניחו כו' וערש"י שם אבל תוס' בבכורות שם ד"ה במקום כו' כתבו דא"צ ע"ש וכן מצינו כמה אמוראי בבבל שהיו מתירין בכורות ביחידי ואפשר ע"י נטילת רשות וגם דברי תוס' י"ל כן שלא אמרו אלא שא"צ סמוך כמ"ש ביומא שם שאינו אלא משום כבודו של נשיא ומיהו עכשיו שאין נשיא אפשר שא"צ וז"ש תוס' שם ד"ה פסק ומיהו בזה"ז אין נראה כו' משמע אבל משום נטילת רשות אין קפידא וכן הרא"ש בהלכותיו סוף בכורות והאידנא שאין חכם ומומחה כו' שאין בקיאין בהן האידנא ואמר חכם ומומחה כנ"ל וכמ"ש בפ"ה סי"א וכתב הר"י כו' ובדו"פ כתב ב' הטעמים של ב"י וכתבו בשם הרא"ש וטעה בזה ונמשך אחר דברי ב"י:

beur_hagra.en:
Even. Tosafot, Bechorot 36b, and the Mishnah and Gemara there.
By an expert... and if there is none. This is stated there. (Likkut) And if there is none. This follows the first Tanna and the Gemara there, Bechorot 37a, and the end of chapter 3 of Shabbos.
And nowadays. Rosh and Tosafot there explain that a true expert must be both a great scholar and especially proficient in examining blemishes. This is why the Gemara distinguishes between a chacham for vows and a mumcheh for a firstborn. Beit Yosef gives an additional reason: there is no nasi in Eretz Yisrael nowadays from whom authorization can be obtained, based on Rambam's statement at the beginning of chapter 3 that a firstborn is examined by an expert authorized by the nasi of Eretz Yisrael. It appears that Beit Yosef inferred this from the term mumcheh, as in the beginning of Sanhedrin concerning fines that require ordained judges. But there is no proof, because Sanhedrin 5a also calls one who judges alone a mumcheh even without formal authorization. Another possible inference is from Bechorot concerning permitting a firstborn outside Eretz Yisrael. Rambam writes similarly. Rashi, however, explains there that the concern is that the animal is not fit for sacrifice, not lack of authorization. Nor is there proof from Sanhedrin, where the phrase "he may permit firstborn animals" appears alongside "he may issue rulings," since that passage concerns a student who requires authorization because of a particular incident, as discussed above in siman 242. There is, however, a Yerushalmi in which Rav asked Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi, after his father's death, for permission to permit firstborn animals. Ordinarily, after one's teacher dies one no longer requires permission. Yoma 78a likewise recounts that they asked an elder about such authority. Tosafot in Bechorot nevertheless write that formal authorization is unnecessary. We also find many Amoraim in Babylonia who permitted firstborn animals individually. Perhaps they had received authorization. Tosafot's words can also be understood as saying only that semikhah is unnecessary, while authorization out of respect for the nasi remains required. Nowadays, when there is no nasi, perhaps even that is unnecessary. This is suggested by Tosafot's wording that in our time there is no sufficiently qualified expert, implying that authorization itself is not the obstacle. Rosh likewise writes at the end of Bechorot that nowadays there is no chacham and mumcheh because people are not sufficiently expert in blemishes. The two reasons reported in Derishah as though both were from Rosh are therefore mistaken and stem from Beit Yosef's discussion.
It’s not just a quaint. My son and m there:
Like a qua. A gift there:
And a notch. Rosh writes in the name of Ri that a notched ear is an obvious blemish. He infers this from the Gemara's frequent use of the case of one who notches a firstborn's ear, including Bava Kamma 98a and Bechorot 34b. Rambam, however, lists only the three blemishes mentioned earlier, and the Mishnah likewise lists only those three. Why then does it not include a notched ear? The Gemara's use of a notched ear may simply be because it is the first blemish listed in the Mishnah. According to Ri, who permits relying on a notched ear, the same applies to any blemish clearly recognizable without specialized expertise, even if an ordinary person does not know that halachah regards it as a blemish. The need for an expert is due to practical proficiency, not abstract scholarship. Rosh therefore lists in chapter 6 several such blemishes, and Tur records them here. He explains that non-obvious blemishes include cataracts of the eye and similar defects. Rambam disagrees and follows his own position that the problem is authorization, so only a blemish universally known may be acted upon without an expert. Rosh follows his own position. The Shulchan Aruch is therefore difficult, because it combines Rambam's approach with Ri's and assumes that a notched ear is considered universally obvious even according to Rambam. That is not so. Are the other blemishes listed by Rosh any less obvious than a notched ear? Rosh mentioned a notched ear only to teach the novelty that it too counts as an obvious blemish, whereas Shulchan Aruch omitted the other blemishes Rosh and Tur listed and retained only the notched ear.
Which is more. Meaning that nowadays the blemish must be more readily visible to the eye. By strict law, however, it is enough that the fingernail catches upon it, as stated in the Gemara there and in the first chapter of Chullin. Regarding the definition of a blemish that catches the fingernail, see what I wrote at the beginning of siman 18 in the name of Rashba and Raah, who disagree on the point.
Through a deficiency. See Rashi on the Mishnah there, Bechorot 37a, concerning a chip. The same applies to a crack, as the Mishnah there says concerning a split, and the Gemara explains that even the slightest crack qualifies. Rosh and Tur write likewise. Shulchan Aruch, however, mentions only a notched ear, which is a form of deficiency, as explained above.
